IDV11: Reactor cooling-water inlet temperature random variation
reasoning: The dominant anomaly is XMEAS_9 (reactor temperature) with max|z|=10.06, an order of magnitude larger than any other column, pointing to a failure of reactor heat removal rather than a feed or condenser-side fault. Secondary shifts in A feed (XMEAS_1/XMV_3), D feed (XMEAS_2), purge A content (XMEAS_23) and separator temperature (XMEAS_11) are consistent with a step rise in reactor cooling-water inlet temperature: hotter cooling water raises reactor temperature, the reaction rate increases, and the controllers compensate via feed and purge adjustments, while the strong XMEAS~XMV correlations (r≈1.0) merely reflect closed-loop control pairings. Condenser/stripper and Stream 4 ratio/composition faults (IDV1/2/5/12/15) would lead with condenser or separator variables instead, so the reactor-cooling family IDV4 > IDV11 > IDV14 is the ranked conclusion.
